handbookNote: Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries (LDWF) boating education and boating safety program (wlf.louisiana.gov) -- Louisiana has no single official state-administered boating knowledge exam; LDWF's own boater education page requires individuals born after January 1, 1984 to complete an approved boater education course before operating a motorboat exceeding 10 horsepower or a personal watercraft, with recognized exemptions for those accompanied by a person 18+ who has completed the course and for U.S. Coast Guard-licensed captains -- this mandate and its birth-date cutoff were independently confirmed by two sources: LDWF's own boater-education page (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/boater-education), which states the January 1, 1984 cutoff and vessel/HP scope directly and describes course options (in-person courses taught by LDWF agents/volunteer instructors requiring a 70%+ score, and approved third-party online providers including Boat-Ed.com, BoatUS.org, and Recademics.com), and Boat-Ed's official Louisiana course page (boat-ed.com/louisiana), which independently corroborates the same January 1, 1984 birth-date threshold, the 10-hp/PWC scope, and requires at least 70% on unit quizzes and at least 80% on the final certification exam with unlimited retake attempts to earn the Louisiana Boater Card -- in practice this means the LDWF-approved course vendor's own embedded quizzes and final exam ARE the de facto qualifying test, not a separate LDWF-run exam; exam-format convergence across approved vendors was also checked against BoatUS.org's Louisiana course, which independently confirms a 60-question final exam and a 3-5 hour, 5-lesson course structure, though it does not publish its own passing-percentage figure -- the exact final-exam question count is therefore reported as 60 per BoatUS.org rather than asserted as a universal cross-vendor figure, since Boat-Ed does not itself publish a fixed question count; content is grounded in real Louisiana-specific detail independently verified against LDWF's own published pages: required safety equipment including PFD carriage rules (one wearable PFD per person, a Type IV throwable device for vessels 16 feet and over, mandatory PFD wear for children 16 and younger on vessels under 26 feet, and mandatory wearable-PFD-only rules for PWC riders and towed watersports participants), fire extinguisher/ventilation/muffler/visual-distress-signal requirements scaled by vessel class (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/required-boating-equipment), boating regulations covering PWC-specific restrictions (minimum age 16, prohibitions on weaving through traffic, wake-jumping with obstructed visibility, and wildlife harassment), safe-speed and no-wake-zone rules, BUI parity with Louisiana's highway 0.08% DUI standard, water-skiing observer/mirror rules (7-by-14-inch wide-angle convex mirror exception for a solo operator 16+), and Wildlife Agent termination-order enforcement authority (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/boating-regulations), vessel registration/titling procedures including the three-year registration term, 60-day renewal grace period, $26 titling fee, and 25-hp/financed/homemade/incorrect-HIN titling triggers (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/title-or-register-your-boat), boating accident reporting thresholds (death/injury/disappearance/$500+ property damage/total vessel loss), the 5-day written Incident Report Form deadline, the 800-442-2511 LDWF Law Enforcement Division number, and the Baton Rouge PO Box mailing address (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/report-boat-crash-collision-or-casualty), and LDWF's own boating-safety guidance on bayou/marsh/wetland hazards (shallows, stumps, debris, shifting channels), float plans, and cold-water/hypothermia precautions (wlf.louisiana.gov/page/boating-safety) -- plus universal NASBLA-aligned boating-safety fundamentals (Inland Navigation Rules, the U.S. and Uniform State Aids to Navigation systems, PFD types, required federal equipment, cold-water immersion, hurricane/Gulf storm awareness, and towed water sports safety) applied to Louisiana's exceptional per-capita boat-registration culture, its extensive bayou and coastal-marsh waterway network, Mississippi River commercial tow traffic, and its hurricane-exposed Gulf coast -- price matches this project's
